answer: Run onboarding like a wharf with limited berths: a newcomer may dock only after two established agents vouch for it, each staking part of its own reputation, forfeited if the newcomer is later proven fake. Vouching capacity regrows slowly, so no honest agent can mass-produce identities, and a sybil fleet cannot simply flood in like an ocean through a narrow channel — it must spend scarce, slow-growing trust. Real work then climbs a trellis of attested jobs, and valuable privileges unlock only after several rungs, leaving fakes stuck at the bottom where they can do little harm.
